explanations.explanation: "Spoken" is the word, friend. The LORD says, "For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has." (Job 42:7) Eliphaz and his two friends had done a LOT of talking in this story, and now the LORD weighs in on what they said.

Nobody was writing anything down here. It was all talk, and plenty of it. The LORD says, "For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has." (Job 42:7) So the word is "spoken," not "written."

I would pay good money to hear Eliphaz sing, but that's not what the text says. The LORD says, "For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has." (Job 42:7) The word is "spoken." Nobody in this scene is carrying a tune.

That's it, baker! The LORD says, "Then My servant Job will pray for you…" (Job 42:8) Think about that. The friends who talked at Job for chapter after chapter now need him to pray for them. The LORD says He will accept Job's prayer.

Oil is a good guess, but it's not in this verse. The LORD says, "Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer…" (Job 42:8) So Job's part is prayer. The friends bring the animals, and Job brings the prayer.
No towel and no basin in this scene, friend. The LORD says, "Then My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer…" (Job 42:8) Job's job is prayer, and the LORD says He will accept it.

I get why you went there, but it's the opposite. The LORD says Job will pray for them, "for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly." (Job 42:8) So after Job prays, the LORD will NOT deal with them according to their folly. The answer is False.

Yes, baker, False! The LORD says Job will pray for them, "for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you according to your folly." (Job 42:8) The friends brought the offering, and the LORD says He will not deal with them according to their folly. I think that's a big relief for three men who just heard the word "wrath."

Right, baker! The three friends go and do as the LORD told them, "and the LORD accepted Job's prayer." (Job 42:9) That matches what the LORD said earlier: "I will accept his prayer." (Job 42:8) The friends obeyed, and the prayer was accepted.

No refusing here, friend. The text says the friends did as the LORD told them, "and the LORD accepted Job's prayer." (Job 42:9) The LORD had already said, "I will accept his prayer." (Job 42:8) So the word is "accepts."
Nobody gets ignored in this verse. The friends did as the LORD told them, "and the LORD accepted Job's prayer." (Job 42:9) The LORD said it would happen, and then it did. The word is "accepts."

Yes, baker! "After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions." (Job 42:10) Notice the order. Job prays for his friends, and then the restoring comes. Restored, and then doubled, too.

Job already went through the removing, friend. This verse goes the other way. "After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions." (Job 42:10) The word is "restores."

Nothing is being held back here. "After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions." (Job 42:10) "Withholds" is the opposite of what happens. The word is "restores."

explanations.answer: A piece of silver and a gold ring
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker! "And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring." (Job 42:11) His brothers, his sisters and everyone who knew him from before came to the meal. They consoled him and comforted him, and each one brought a gift.

explanations.answer: A young lamb and a jar of oil
explanations.explanation: Close to a gift basket, but no lamb and no oil. The text says, "And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring." (Job 42:11) That's the gift from every single guest. They also consoled and comforted him over all the adversity.

explanations.answer: A new robe and a pair of sandals
explanations.explanation: A nice outfit, friend, but that's not what they brought. "And each one gave him a piece of silver and a gold ring." (Job 42:11) Every guest came with a piece of silver and a gold ring.

True, baker! "So the LORD blessed Job's latter days more than his first." (Job 42:12) Then the verse lists what Job owned. After everything he went through, the LORD blessed the latter days even more than the first.

I see why you'd pause after all Job went through, but the text says it plainly. "So the LORD blessed Job's latter days more than his first." (Job 42:12) The statement is True. Job's later days were blessed even more than his earlier ones.

Right, baker! "…their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers." (Job 42:15) Job had seven sons and three daughters, and the daughters received an inheritance among their brothers. The text puts that right beside the names Jemimah, Keziah and Keren-happuch.

A house would be nice, friend, but the text doesn't say that. It says, "…their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers." (Job 42:15) The gift was an inheritance, shared in the middle of the family.

That's a fancy guess, but the text doesn't mention any seat. It says, "…their father granted them an inheritance among their brothers." (Job 42:15) So the gift was an inheritance, and they got it right alongside their brothers.

That's it, baker! "After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation." (Job 42:16) That's children, grandchildren and on down the line. Job lived to see a whole family tree.

The text goes further than that, friend. "After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation." (Job 42:16) Second would just be his children, and Job saw more. It's the fourth generation.

That's a LOT of family reunions, friend, but the text says less. "After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation." (Job 42:16) Job saw to the fourth generation. That's still a full house at the holidays.
